original.target_description: Original primary experiment; locator p. 9 and broad description do not distinguish separate group-specific urge/purchase correlations, their difference, or group-by-purchase-status ANOVA interaction and follow-up contrasts. Purchasing-frequency and Card 2 urge analyses also fit the description on pp. 7–8.

n.sample_role: Target analytic sample unresolved; participant-count candidates only in notes and dispositions.
n.exclusions: One procedural exclusion from all analyses; six additional participants excluded from urge analyses for incomplete or missing urge ratings (pp. 4, 7).
n.location: PDF-text p. 9, Relationship Between Urge and Purchase Status; p. 7, Purchasing Behaviour and Analytical Strategy
n.quote:
For the near-miss group, urge ratings immediately following the near-
miss were significantly positively correlated with purchasing status, rpb = .49, n = 29,
p = .007. For the loss group, however, urge ratings following the loss showed no rela-
tionship with purchasing status, rpb = -.018, n = 29, p = .926.

es.location: PDF-text p. 9, Relationship Between Urge and Purchase Status
es.quote:
A between-subjects ANOVA, with group and purchase status as the between-
subjects variables indicated a significant interaction between group and purchase status,
F(1, 54) = 4.90, p = .031, g2p = .083.

notes: Identity verified independently from first-page title, authors Madison Stange, Candice Graydon, Mike J. Dixon, DOI 10.1007/s10899-016-9662-2, and ORIGINAL PAPER designation. Full article text includes Methods, Results, Discussion and References; primary report, not an abstract or preregistration. No PDF was supplied. Only original n_o and es_value_o assigned; replication, original p and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Target ambiguity: p. 9 contains near-miss urge/purchase correlation rpb = .49, n = 29, p = .007; loss correlation rpb = -.018, n = 29, p = .926; correlation comparison Z = 1.99, p = .046; group-by-purchase-status interaction F(1, 54) = 4.90, p = .031, g2p = .083 (canonical extraction of partial eta-squared); follow-ups loss t(27) = .09, p = .926 and near-miss t(27) = 2.92, p = .007. Metric requested etasq does not independently establish which target test was intended or justify converting partial eta-squared to eta-squared. Candidate analytic participant counts: each group-specific correlation explicitly n = 29. The mutually exclusive loss and near-miss groups in the urge/purchase analyses yield candidate common urge-model N: 29 + 29 = 58; this is not assigned to n_o because row-specific target correspondence is unresolved. Exclusions are one procedural exclusion and six incomplete/missing urge evaluations from 65 recruits. Purchasing-frequency test instead explicitly has N = 64, X2 (1, N = 64) = .829, p = .362 (p. 7). No N inferred from df. Other description-compatible tests on p. 8 include Card 2 group F(1, 56) = 4.07, p = .049, g2p = .068; game-by-group F(1.78, 99.85) = 18.96, p < .001, g2p = .253; game 3 near-miss/loss contrast t(56) = 4.04, p < .001. These are candidates only; no effect-size conversion performed.
